observations: Built a standalone forward-only collector (examples/qasper2/train/collect_bg_stats.py) that loads the Phase-1 self-distilled Qwen3-4B cartridge (cache_last.pt: 511 trainable + 1 frozen tokens, 36 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128) and the Phase-1 QA PRESERVE corpus (qwen_qasper_QA_task_8192.parquet), then calls cartridges.sparse_cache_finetuning.collect_background_stats(is_ddp=False) to save a BackgroundAccessTracker at per_layer granularity. The EXP-002 sketch's imports/signatures were all confirmed against source (collect_background_stats params, SparseCacheFinetuningConfig fields, TrainDataset.Config/DataSource, CacheAndModel(cache,model) with no am/sparse config so collect installs its own query-capture hooks). Two adaptations vs the sketch: (1) NUM_BG_BATCHES set to 999999999 (not 1000) so the full QA corpus is covered -- the map-style TrainDataset DataLoader stops after one epoch = 1990 packed sequences (the sketch's 1000 would have truncated coverage, as the older initial_am bg_stats did); (2) the cache must be moved with .to(local_rank) AFTER TrainableCache.from_pretrained(device='cuda') -- from_pretrained map_location's the loaded weights but the internally-constructed _seq_ids/_init_seq_ids buffers stay on CPU, causing a cuda-vs-cpu device error in create_block_mask_w_cache on the first forward; the validated continual_am_sparse.py does this extra .to(local_rank), which I mirrored (one-line fix after an initial crash). SANITY CHECK passed: bg_stats.pt loads with keys {batch_ranked_positions, num_batches, granularity}, shape (1990, 36, 511) int64 spanning all 36 layers and 511 trainable slots, num_batches=1990, granularity=per_layer. The check reconstructed the file via the EXACT Phase-2 path -- BackgroundAccessTracker(num_batches=..., granularity='per_layer').load(path) then CacheTFIDFRanker(background_tracker=..., use_idf=True, smoothing=1.0, top_k_per_batch=128, granularity='per_layer') -- yielding a finite IDF of shape (36, 511) with min/mean/max = 0.0000/2.4730/7.5964 and document frequencies in [0, 1990]; so continual_am_sparse.py's bg_tracker.load() WILL accept this file (USE_IDF=1 + BG_STATS_PATH=outputs/phase1_selfdistill_qwen512/bg_stats.pt, GRANULARITY=per_layer). Caveats: collect_wallclock_s=265.3s is dominated by the cold flex_attention torch.compile of the first forward (~4+ min, CPU-bound, contending with the concurrent EXP-000 job on GPU0); a warm re-run would be far faster. The collect_background_stats 'Collecting background stats' / 'Background collection: N/M' logger.info lines are buffered and never reach the redirected log file -- only the script's own print(flush=True) markers (COLLECT_WALLCLOCK_S, SANITY, RESULT, DONE) and the saved file are reliable progress signals; this is cosmetic, the collection itself is complete and correct. bg_stats.pt is 292,866,032 bytes (matches 1990*36*511*8).
